statement: In shortest path algorithms on a weighted digraph, relaxation updates the tentative distance to a vertex v along edge (u, v) with weight w by v.distance := min(v.distance, u.distance + w). For a shortest path P from source s to v with final edge uv, if u.distance is at most the shortest path length using at most i - 1 edges, relaxation guarantees v.distance is at most the shortest path length using at most i edges, and at termination in a graph with no negative-weight cycles, every edge satisfies v.distance <= u.distance + uv.weight.

steps.text: For the base case i = 0 before the edge relaxation loop executes, initialize source.distance := 0 and u.distance := infinity for all u != source, which is correct because no path from source to u exists with 0 edges.

For the inductive step, consider when a vertex distance is updated by relaxation: v.distance := u.distance + uv.weight. If by induction u.distance is the length of some path from source to u, then u.distance + uv.weight is the length of the path from source to v obtained by following the path from source to u and appending edge uv.

Let P be a shortest path from source to v with at most i edges, and let u be the last vertex before v on P. The subpath of P from source to u must be a shortest path from source to u with at most i - 1 edges; otherwise, a strictly shorter path to u could be concatenated with edge uv to form a path to v with at most i edges strictly shorter than P, yielding a contradiction.

By inductive hypothesis, u.distance after i - 1 iterations is at most the length of the subpath from source to u, so uv.weight + u.distance <= length(P). In the i-th iteration, v.distance is compared with uv.weight + u.distance and set equal to it if smaller, ensuring that after i iterations v.distance <= length(P), the shortest path length using at most i edges.

If no negative-weight cycles exist, every shortest path visits each vertex at most once (using at most |V| - 1 edges), so after |V| - 1 iterations no further distance improvements can be made. Therefore, for any cycle with vertices v[0], ..., v[k-1], every edge satisfies v[i].distance <= v[i-1 (mod k)].distance + v[i-1 (mod k)]v[i].weight.

Summing the relaxation inequality around the cycle from i = 1 to k, the v[i].distance and v[i-1 (mod k)].distance terms cancel, leaving 0 <= sum_{i=1}^k v[i-1 (mod k)]v[i].weight, establishing that the termination of relaxation implies every cycle has non-negative weight.

assumptions.assumption: The weighted graph contains no negative-weight cycles reachable from the source vertex.
assumptions.breaks_when: A reachable cycle has negative total weight, allowing distances to be made arbitrarily small by repeated traversals so that no shortest path exists.

assumptions.assumption: Tentative distances are initialized to infinity for all non-source vertices and 0 for the source vertex.
assumptions.breaks_when: Initial values underestimate true path costs or fail to properly distinguish the source from other vertices.

assumptions.assumption: Edge weights are non-negative when greedy single-edge relaxation order without full passes is used.
assumptions.breaks_when: Negative edge weights cause greedy frontier settlement to permanently settle vertices with suboptimal tentative distances.

failure_modes.signature: Relaxation condition distance[u] + w < distance[v] remains satisfied on some edge after |V| - 1 iterations
failure_modes.cause: A cycle whose edge weights sum to a negative value enables path lengths to decrease indefinitely upon repeated traversal

failure_modes.signature: Halting search immediately when forward and backward search frontiers meet, resulting in a suboptimal path length mu > delta(s, t)
failure_modes.cause: A shorter connecting path crossing elsewhere between search frontiers exists before the queue priority sum reaches mu

failure_modes.mode: Count to infinity in distributed distance-vector routing
failure_modes.signature: Nodes spend forever gradually increasing distance estimates while routing loops persist
failure_modes.cause: Node or link failure isolates a destination while updates propagate node-by-node without rapid topology reflection

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, the smacplannerhybrid component relies on shortest path graph search to generate kinematically feasible vehicle trajectories. Edge relaxation is the core mechanism used during node expansion to update tentative cost-to-come values across neighbor states. This guarantees that path costs monotonically decrease toward the optimal shortest path from the start pose.
